title: Triangle closure of bounded-target internal-Hom continuity
statement: Let $(\mathcal C,\mathcal O)$ be a ringed site small in the chosen universe [def-weil-pbc-sites-and-cohomology, def-weil-size-convention], with $\mathcal O$ commutative. Use $D(\mathcal O)$, the ordinary unbounded derived category of sheaves of $\mathcal O$-modules [def-weil-abstract-derived-category, def-weil-sheaf-of-modules-category], and $H(A,N)=R\mathcal Hom_{\mathcal O}(A,N)$ [def-pur-derived-internal-hom]. For a source $A$ write $P(A)$ when for every small filtered diagram $(N_i)$ of complexes [def-weil-pbc-category-colimit] with $H^{<c}(N_i)=0$ for a common integer $c$, the canonical map $\varinjlim_iH(A,N_i)\to H(A,\varinjlim_iN_i)$ is an isomorphism, and there exists $d_A\in\mathbf Z$ such that $H(A,N)\in D^{\ge c+d_A}$ whenever $N\in D^{\ge c}$, for every $c,N$ [def-sbc-standard-tstructure-derived-category]. Colimits mean exact termwise sheaf colimits of functorial complex models; the maps come from evaluation and the target cocone. Then $P(0)$ holds, $P$ is invariant under source isomorphism, and the sources satisfying $P$ are closed under shifts and two-out-of-three in distinguished triangles [def-weil-triangulated-category]. One may take $d_{A[n]}=d_A+n$. Consequently they are closed under any finite construction from such sources using shifts, triangles and isomorphisms.

source.place: Tag 08JC (lemma-RHom-triangulated); agent extraction of the bounded-target continuity subcategory used in Bhatt–Scholze Lemmas 6.3.14 and 6.8.12.

proof.text: For zero source the Hom-complex terms are products of zero sheaves, so $H(0,N)=0$, its comparison is $0\to0$, and $d_0=0$ [def-pur-derived-internal-hom]. Source isomorphisms identify comparisons by [lem-sfb-rhom-colimit-source-transport] and identify bounds by bifunctoriality; hence $P$ is isomorphism invariant.

By [lem-sfb-rhom-colimit-source-transport], the comparison for $A[n]$ is conjugate to $\alpha_A[-n]$. Thus continuity is preserved. Its source-shift isomorphism gives $H^q(H(A[n],N))=H^{q-n}(H(A,N))$, so $q<c+d_A+n$ implies vanishing. Hence $d_{A[n]}=d_A+n$ [def-sbc-standard-tstructure-derived-category].

For a distinguished $A\to B\to C\to A[1]$ with $P(A),P(C)$ and a uniformly bounded-below filtered target diagram, use [lem-sfb-rhom-colimit-cohomology-ladder]. At every $q$ its five terms indexed $(A,q-1),(C,q),(B,q),(A,q),(C,q+1)$ give exact rows and commuting squares. The four outer verticals are isomorphisms by the two continuity assumptions. The five lemma [lem-weil-pbc-five-lemma] makes the middle one an isomorphism. The ladder identifies it with the cohomology of the actual comparison chain map, which is therefore a quasi-isomorphism; its localization $\alpha_B$ is an isomorphism [def-weil-abstract-derived-category].

For $N\in D^{\ge c}$ the contravariant Hom triangle [lem-weil-pbc-ringed-internal-hom-exact-restriction] has exact cohomology [lem-sf-derived-homology-long-exact]. In $H^qH(C,N)\to H^qH(B,N)\to H^qH(A,N)$ both outer terms vanish for $q<c+\min(d_A,d_C)$, hence so does the middle. Thus $d_B=\min(d_A,d_C)$ is uniform in $c,N$ [def-sbc-standard-tstructure-derived-category], proving $P(B)$.

source.place: Tag 08JC and Derived Categories Tag 05RS; old step 6

proof.text: Rotate the original triangle using [def-weil-triangulated-category]. If $P(B),P(C)$ hold, its inverse rotation is $C[-1]\to A\to B\to C$, and steps 2--4 give $P(A)$, with $d_A=\min(d_C-1,d_B)$. If $P(A),P(B)$ hold, its rotation is $B\to C\to A[1]\to B[1]$, giving $P(C)$ with $d_C=\min(d_B,d_A+1)$. The rotation signs do not affect either the isomorphism or vanishing assertions. This proves two-out-of-three in every position.

Induct on the length of a finite construction. Initial sources have $P$ by assumption; zero is covered by step 1. Each subsequent isomorphism, shift or triangle operation preserves $P$ by steps 1,2 or 3--5 respectively. This proves the final assertion.

lean.statement: theorem boundedTargetHomContinuous_triangle_closure : ObjectProperty.IsClosedUnderIsomorphisms (BoundedTargetHomContinuous.{c, v, r, w} J R) ∧ ObjectProperty.IsTriangulated (BoundedTargetHomContinuous.{c, v, r, w} J R) ∧ (∀ (A : D.{c, v, r, w} J R), BoundedTargetHomContinuous.{c, v, r, w} J R A → ∀ d : ℤ, (∀ (b : ℤ) (N : D.{c, v, r, w} J R), N.IsGE b → ((hom.{c, v, r, w} J R A).obj N).IsGE (b + d)) → ∀ (n b : ℤ) (N : D.{c, v, r, w} J R), N.IsGE b → ((hom.{c, v, r, w} J R (A⟦n⟧)).obj N).IsGE (b + (d + n))) ∧ (∀ S : ObjectProperty (D.{c, v, r, w} J R), S ≤ BoundedTargetHomContinuous.{c, v, r, w} J R → ∀ n : ℕ, (S.shiftClosure ℤ).extensionProductIter n ≤ BoundedTargetHomContinuous.{c, v, r, w} J R)
